name: hirokata
description: A curated collection of Claude Code plugins for enhanced development workflows

plugins.name: software
plugins.description: Requirements-to-implementation workflow with 8-phase clean architecture, automated planning, adaptive parallel execution, intelligent conventional commit generation, and comprehensive requirements documentation.

plugins.name: guild
plugins.description: Continuous agent orchestration on a Turso-backed board where status is a column, not a directory. The chain is DATA: a YAML template instantiated per requirement into an execution graph, with exactly two gates — the plan is approved before anything is built, and findings, bugs and failures are presented together as one decision after review. 'guild segment' says what runs next; a ticket names a required CAPABILITY rather than an agent, so any roster member whose declared capabilities cover it is eligible and adding an agent file is the whole of hiring. It can work a shift while you are away — 'guild shift' claims bounties, runs segments, retries a failure once, commits per completed task on its own branch, and stops at the next gate, because a gate is the one decision no subagent can make; it never pushes and never touches the default branch. 'guild brief' says where the project stands, 'guild shift-report' says what moved overnight, and 'guild dashboard' renders the board as one offline HTML page, while an independent QA discipline files bugs and maps risk coverage as rows. Recovery is a journal replay. Say 'check in' to start a work session, or 'work a shift' to leave it running.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: PhD-level multi-perspective research inspired by Stanford's STORM. The 'storm research' skill orchestrates five expert persona agents (practitioner, skeptic, economist, historian, academic), maps their contradictions, synthesizes a cited briefing, and red-teams the result. Say 'storm research <topic>' to start.

plugins.name: storytelling
plugins.description: Turn any idea, pitch, update, or decision into a message that lands using six proven storytelling frameworks (Simon Sinek's Golden Circle, Minto's Pyramid Principle, the Pixar Pitch, StoryBrand, What/So What/Now What, and ABT). The 'storytelling' skill diagnoses your audience and goal, recommends the right framework, and drafts the message — in parallel across frameworks when the framing is uncertain. Each framework is also a standalone skill. Say 'help me tell the story of <X>' to start.
